answer: A raven that croaks the same fable every morning and a sparrow that sings once a season should not earn the same trust. Give every identity a reputation score that decays unless it keeps doing useful, verifiable work over time, and weight brand-new identities near zero. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities gains nothing at first, and must pay the ongoing cost of real work for each one before any of them can vote, attest, or earn — the Sybil army starves before it can act.
